source.title: Sequence-Dropout Block for Reducing Overfitting Problem in Image Classification
source.authors: Le-Dan Qian; Li-Bing Hu; Li Zhao; Tao Wang; Run-Hua Jiang

record.tranche_reason: Tests dropout’s effect on held-out performance with comparisons against no regularization and other regularizers, using its own sequence-dropout method as well.
record.gate_note: The study reports dropout results on MNIST classifiers and compares regularizers on MNIST. Other benchmark comparisons of sequence-dropout with dropout do not establish dropout’s effect against no dropout. A synthetic regression experiment is outside the classifier versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares standard dropout with no dropout on MNIST using held-out classification accuracy, the method and measure relevant to V6. Table 2 and Figure 3 also compare fully connected and convolutional classifiers, potentially bearing on V3, but the supplied text omits the CNN accuracies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that sequence-dropout reduces overfitting and improves performance relative to standard dropout in their reported comparisons, with broad applicability across five image-classification datasets.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a sequence-based feature-channel dropout block; experiments compare it with standard dropout and other regularizers.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model architecture vary across experiments. Dropout outcomes on the MNIST CNN are shown in a figure without a textual value.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic regression with 30 sampled points, dropout has test loss 0.2660 versus 0.3485 without regularization; sequence-dropout achieves 0.1919.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout can improve held-out regression loss on a small synthetic dataset.

record.problems: The study gives no uncertainty estimates. The text does not provide the MNIST CNN dropout accuracy, referring to a figure instead. The regularization comparison does not state the no-regularization error in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. The study also reports sequence-dropout comparisons on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet2012, Places365-Standard, and synthetic regression; these do not directly measure the dropout effect against an unregularized classifier baseline described by V6.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.

The contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, and initialization from a trained convolutional network. The basic MNIST architecture comparison is present but cannot be evaluated numerically from the supplied text.
Controlled comparisons of adaptive optimizers with SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.

Very small classifier training sets, excessive dropout, and jointly removing dropout and weight decay with data augmentation. The small synthetic regression experiment does not test the classifier claim.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: The no-regularization validation error needed to compare with R2's dropout error of 0.66%. No verdict on this comparison is possible from the supplied text.
CNN accuracy with and without standard dropout. The experiment is described, but the supplied text provides neither the numerical difference nor its direction.

Matched MLP-versus-CNN held-out accuracies, particularly without dropout, to evaluate the architecture comparison. The MLP baseline is 98.06%; the CNN value is unavailable, so no V3 verdict can be assigned.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for the claim versions. Numerical table bodies and figure curves are absent from the supplied text; their values cannot be inferred from captions. Sequence-dropout's superiority to standard dropout does not itself establish standard dropout's benefit over no dropout.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks under the specified comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD on classification or language benchmarks.
Large-batch training and its generalization gap.

No reported experiment tests the effect of dropout on very small training sets or the effect of too much dropout. The MNIST classifier results do not report a dropout comparison for the CNN in text; a figure is provided.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.check: The values are correct: accuracy increases from 98.06% to 98.09%, equivalent to error falling from 1.94% to 1.91%. This is a small improvement; no uncertainty or significance assessment is reported.
